question: Read the first Form 990 of Giving Block Foundation (EIN 92-3363254, Miami; IRS ruling 2024-12, care of The Giving Block) when it appears in the IRS TEOS index (TY2025; not indexed at 2026-11-20): Part VIII 1g, Schedule M crypto and securities lines and counts, Schedule I recipients, and whether Schedule D is filed. Test 'approximately 2,400 charities' (Shift4 FY2025 10-K) and the self-reported 'over $100 million' of 2025 crypto against filed dollars
conclusion_affected: Size of the nonprofit-side crypto intake market; whether The Giving Block routes gifts through its own charity
rationale: Shift4 discloses no Giving Block volume (26 earnings releases 2020-Q2 to 2026-Q3 never mention it; stock donations are folded into $209bn of FY2025 volume) and the new foundation is the only filing route left

question: FreeWill Impact Fund (EIN 86-1218871) TY2025 Form 990 when indexed: repeat the Schedule M crypto/securities split and Schedule I concentration; check whether a single grant to a DAF sponsor again dominates (TY2024: $5,430,494 to The Oregon Community Foundation, 45.7% of contributions) and whether the TY2023 Schedule M counts (750 and 750) are placeholders
conclusion_affected: Realised Crypto for Charity volume and its lumpiness; double counting of vendor intake that is regranted into DAF sponsors
rationale: TY2024 intake doubled to $11.89m (crypto $7.63m in 648 gifts) but half went to one community foundation; TY2023 counts are identical in both classes

question: Overflow's affiliated charities: read the Form 990/990-EZ returns of Overflow Foundation Inc (EIN 83-3654557, 990-EZ TY2020-23, 990 TY2024) and Overflow Foundation (EIN 88-3232461, 990 TY2023-24) for Schedule M stock/crypto lines, Schedule I recipient counts and fees, to test Overflow's '>450 organisations' and '$12,979 average stock gift' claims

question: The Giving Block 2026 annual report: reconcile '22,343 donations' x '$11,019 average' (= $246.2m) with the headline 'over $100 million' of 2025 crypto, using the downloadable PDF of the report and its methodology notes (public pages only)
conclusion_affected: Which Giving Block volume figure to cite in market sizing
rationale: The two figures on the same page differ by a factor of 2.46; the 'one in five nonprofits raised over $100,000' line implies at least $48m with ~2,400 charities

question: Screen the outside-DAFRC universe for self-described DAF charities that file no Schedule D: Form 990 filers whose mission, Part III or Schedule O text contains 'donor advised fund' while Part IV line 6 is No and Schedule D is absent (pattern of DAFpay Network TY2024-25, FreeWill Impact Fund TY2021-24, DonateStock Charitable FY2025). Count them and sum Part VIII contributions and Part IX grants as an intermediary memo line, flagging receipts that are DAF-sponsor grants
conclusion_affected: Whether any self-described DAF dollars sit outside sponsor and processor totals; rule for the intermediary memo line
rationale: Line 6 screens and DAFRC's Schedule D selection both miss these filers by construction; three were found by hand in this pass

question: DAFRC blank-as-zero audit: count DAFRC panel rows whose Schedule D Part I contributions or grants are 0 with source 'IRS 990' while the matching XML leaves DonorAdvisedFundsContriAmt / DonorAdvisedFundsGrantsAmt blank (DonateStock FY2023 and FY2024 are two such rows), and size the dollars using Part VIII and Part IX as proxies
conclusion_affected: Panel contribution and grant totals; payout ratios for small sponsors
rationale: DonateStock's 0/0 rows hide $5.08m and $12.78m of contributions; the repo harvest already flags sched_d_grants_missing for these returns, so the coding rule is the open question
